language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Sà-wàt-dee and welcome to Thailand. My name is Pim Panyopas and I trade on this floating market in Thailand.
I don’t live near an active volcano, but I hear almost 1 in 10 people do. That is both exciting and scary!

This is what I know about how volcanoes are formed: deep inside the Earth, it is so hot that rocks melt. This melted rock is called magma. Magma rises to the surface of the Earth and if it finds an opening, like a hole on the surface of the Earth, it bursts through.
Let’s float down the river and meet some people to learn more about volcanoes.

Let’s float down the river and meet some people to learn more about volcanoes.
The boat is named 'Vulcan'. The word 'volcano' comes from the blacksmith of the Roman Gods, Vulcan.
Many years ago, people thought that Vulcan created volcanoes.
Volcanoes create and destroy. They can be beneficial to the soil but are generally known for the great destruction they cause.

Wonderful! You are now familiar with some volcanic terms.
Did you know that there are three main types of volcanoes?
The first type of volcanoes are Cinder Cones; they have a single vent which shoots up ash and grainy cinders which land around the vent to form a cone.
The second type are Composite Volcanoes; they are built of layers of lava flow, ash, and unmelted stone. They erupt explosively.
The third type are Shield Volcanoes; they look like a warrior's shield. They are huge, with gentle slopes.
Have a go at matching the features to the correct type of volcano, just for fun!

exercises.title: Movement of Magma in the Mantle

dialog.text: Ah! Now for a rest with my book and a can of soda.

According to my book, magma and lava are the same thing; they are both hot melted rock. It is called 'magma' in the earth's mantle, and 'lava' when it is outside the volcano. Magma contains many gases.

The mantle is a fiery layer of rock under the surface of the Earth. The pressure in the mantle forces the magma toward the crust. When magma is released into the air, it results in explosions, similar to what happens when I open my can of soda.
Now, have a go at these questions.
